A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same theoretical work. Their main text, equations, algorithms and complete appendices are readable, and retained material can be matched across relocations and additions.

before.justification: v1 reports theoretical constructions and proofs. Its Dyck-language examples illustrate the construction rather than report an empirical or simulation study.

after.justification: The new Appendix C announces a Python implementation and links to code and demo results, but reports no experimental outcomes within the PDF. The retained illustrative examples remain theoretical.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 corrects its stopping condition from # to $, matching the output convention already stated in v1. The 2-PTM instructions, tokenizer, CoT execution and Transformer construction otherwise remain unchanged; Appendices B.10–B.11 explain the existing construction.

E1.justification: Neither PDF specifies datasets or tasks used in an empirical evaluation. The Dyck-language illustration is retained, and the new implementation pointer identifies no additional evaluated coverage.

E2.justification: Neither version reports evaluated comparison methods. Added citations and discussion of earlier theoretical constructions do not introduce experimental baselines.

E3.justification: Neither version reports experimental splits, metrics, budgets or testing procedures. Appendix C supplies no evaluation protocol; the new exact-arithmetic assumption concerns the theory.

E4.justification: No ablations, robustness tests, sensitivity studies or empirical case analyses are added or removed. Appendix D discusses theoretical limitations without testing them.

E5.justification: Neither PDF reports repeated runs, seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests or statistical uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: The illustrative Dyck program, execution trace and tokenization example are unchanged. Appendix C adds no measurements, result entries or reported experimental findings.

T1.justification: Theorem 3.1 gains an explicit exact-arithmetic assumption. Appendix B.11 adds a short argument for constant construction size and finite parameter representation, while Appendix D adds conditional reasoning about logarithmic CoT under L != NL. The principal universality and complexity theorems retain their statements and bounds.

C1.justification: The introduction adds a 'Simple construction' contribution, acknowledging that existence can already be deduced by combining prior theorems and emphasizing the explicit construction's simplicity. The abstract and conclusion retain the same universality and complexity claims.

C2.justification: Appendix D substantially expands the applicability discussion: it identifies hardmax versus practical softmax, unbounded versus bounded context windows, and long CoTs for difficult problems as limitations. It also explains the universal-Turing-machine connection. The existing learnability limitation is relocated from the conclusion, not newly introduced.

D1.justification: Appendix C newly identifies a Python implementation and provides a code/demo access link. Appendix B.10 documents how token embeddings, positional information and intermediate results occupy hidden coordinates and are combined through residual connections. These are disclosures about the existing construction.

R1.justification: The introduction and Appendix D materially refine the novelty positioning by acknowledging that Hennie–Stearns and Pérez et al. together imply the existence result, distinguishing the paper's simpler explicit construction. Section 1.1 also substantially expands the cited literature, including Chen et al. (2024) and Qiu & Tong (2024).

P1.justification: v2 makes targeted wording and notation corrections, adjusts the title and publication header, and adds appendix subsections while retaining most existing exposition. The learnability paragraph moves to Appendix D. Appendix A.2 corrects its branch-condition wording from 1 to 0 to agree with the unchanged Equation (37).

P2.justification: Algorithms 1 and 2 move from main-text pages 4 and 7 to a shared appendix-opening page 15. The contents list and surrounding layout expand accordingly, while the single-column presentation remains similar. Neither version contains result figures or tables.

improvement.justification: v2 improves transparency through clearer attribution of the existence result, explicit assumptions, additional construction details and substantive practical limitations. It also resolves local inconsistencies in the pseudocode and branch description. These are useful refinements to largely retained theoretical results and proofs, supporting a limited overall improvement.
